```{r inclass-analysis}
# function to compute tests
test_fn <- function(.df){
  t_test(.df, 
         formula = level ~ group,
         order = c('ASD', 'TD'),
         alternative = 'two-sided',
         var.equal = F)
}

ttests_out <- biomarker_clean %>%
  # drop ADOS score
  select(-ados) %>%
  # arrange in long format
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%
  # nest by protein
  nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  # compute t tests
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  # sort by p-value
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  # multiple testing correction
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)

# select significant proteins
proteins_s1 <- ttests_out %>%
  slice_min(p.adj, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)

## RANDOM FOREST
##################

# store predictors and response separately
predictors <- biomarker_clean %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

response <- biomarker_clean %>% pull(group) %>% factor()

# fit RF
set.seed(101422)
rf_out <- randomForest(x = predictors, 
                       y = response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)

# check errors
rf_out$confusion

# compute importance scores
proteins_s2 <- rf_out$importance %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) %>%
  slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)

## LOGISTIC REGRESSION
#######################

# select subset of interest
proteins_sstar <- intersect(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)

biomarker_sstar <- biomarker_clean %>%
  select(group, any_of(proteins_sstar)) %>%
  mutate(class = (group == 'ASD')) %>%
  select(-group)

biomarker_sstar

# partition into training and test set
set.seed(101422)
biomarker_split <- biomarker_sstar %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

# fit logistic regression model to training set
fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
           data = training(biomarker_split), 
           family = 'binomial')

# evaluate errors on test set
class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)



original_metrics <- testing(biomarker_split) %>%
  add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>% 
  mutate(estimate = factor(pred >0.5, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
         truth = factor(class, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = estimate,
              truth = truth, pred,
              event_level = 'second')

```

```{r remove outlier trimming}
# get names
var_names <- read_csv('../../data/biomarker-raw.csv', 
                     col_names = F, 
                     n_max = 2, 
                     col_select = -(1:2)) %>%
  t() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  rename(name = V1, 
         abbreviation = V2) %>%
  na.omit()

# function for trimming outliers (good idea??)
# trim <- function(x, .at){
#   x[abs(x) > .at] <- sign(x[abs(x) > .at])*.at
#   return(x)
# }

# read in data
biomarker_clean_out <- read_csv('../../data/biomarker-raw.csv', 
         skip = 2,
         col_select = -2L,
         col_names = c('group', 
                       'empty',
                       pull(var_names, abbreviation),
                       'ados'),
         na = c('-', '')) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
  # log transform, center and scale, and trim
  mutate(across(.cols = -c(group, ados),
                ~ scale(log10(.x)))) %>%
  # reorder columns
  select(group, ados, everything())

select_out <- function(x, .at){
  return(x[abs(x) > .at])
}

outliers <- biomarker_clean_out |>
  mutate(subject = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(group, ados, subject),
    names_to = "Proteins",
    values_to = "Values"
  ) |>
  filter(abs(Values) > 3)

outliers_cnt <- biomarker_clean_out |>
  mutate(subject = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(group, ados, subject),
    names_to = "Proteins",
    values_to = "Values"
  ) |>
  group_by(subject, group) |>
  summarise(n_out = sum(abs(Values) > 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(n_out))

outliers_cnt

OutDist_byGroup <- outliers_cnt |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_out, fill = group)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  facet_wrap(~ group) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ASD" = "pink", "TD" = "orange")) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Outliers in Each Subject",
    x = "Number of Outliers (|z| > 3)",
    y = "Count of Subjects"
  )

ggsave(filename = "../../results/figures/OutDist_byGroup.jpg", OutDist_byGroup)

outliers_cnt |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(min = min(n_out),
            max = max(n_out),
            mean = mean(n_out),
            median = median(n_out))
# 152 subjects had outliers
# Highest amount of outliers was 157 for TD and 126 for ASD
# mean outliers was 13 for ASD and 17 for TD
# Both with median of 9 outliers

# TD: 1372 outliers
# ASD: 1007 outliers

# Outliers do not seem to be significantly more prevalant in one group than another. TD marginally has more outliers than ASD.

wilcox.test(n_out ~ group, data = outliers_cnt)
```


```{r repeat analysis}
set.seed(101422)

# For training
partition <- biomarker_clean %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

biomarker_train <- training(partition)
biomarker_test <- testing(partition)

# function to compute tests
test_fn <- function(.df){
  t_test(.df, 
         formula = level ~ group,
         order = c('ASD', 'TD'),
         alternative = 'two-sided',
         var.equal = F)
}


train.ttests_out <- biomarker_train %>%
  # drop ADOS score
  select(-ados) %>%
  # arrange in long format
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%
  # nest by protein
  nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  # compute t tests
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  # sort by p-value
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  # multiple testing correction
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)

n_proteins <- 20

# select significant proteins
train.proteins_s1 <- ttests_out %>%
  slice_min(p.adj, n = n_proteins) %>%
  pull(protein)


## RANDOM FOREST
##################

# store predictors and response separately
train.predictors <- biomarker_train %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

train.response <- biomarker_train %>% pull(group) %>% factor()

# fit RF
train.rf_out <- randomForest(x = train.predictors, 
                       y = train.response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)

# check errors
train.rf_out$confusion

# compute importance scores
train.proteins_s2 <- rf_out$importance %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) %>%
  slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = n_proteins) %>%
  pull(protein)


hard_intersect <- intersect(train.proteins_s1, train.proteins_s2)
fuzzy_intersect <- union(train.proteins_s1, train.proteins_s2)

fuzzy_intersect
## LOGISTIC REGRESSION
#######################

# fit logistic regression model to training set

train.fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
           data = biomarker_train |> mutate(class = (group == "ASD")) |> select(class, all_of(fuzzy_intersect)) , 
           family = 'binomial')

# evaluate errors on test set
class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)

Q3_metrics <- biomarker_test |>
  add_predictions(train.fit, type = 'response') |>
  mutate(estimate = factor(pred >0.5, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
         class = (group == "ASD"),
         truth = factor(class, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = estimate,
              truth = truth, pred,
              event_level = 'second')

original_metrics

Q3_metrics

split_dat_ROC <- biomarker_test |>
```

```{r generalize Q3}
# For training

partition <- biomarker_clean %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

biomarker_train <- training(partition)
biomarker_test <- testing(partition)

# function to compute tests
test_fn <- function(.df){
  t_test(.df, 
         formula = level ~ group,
         order = c('ASD', 'TD'),
         alternative = 'two-sided',
         var.equal = F)
}


train.ttests_out <- biomarker_train %>%
  # drop ADOS score
  select(-ados) %>%
  # arrange in long format
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%
  # nest by protein
  nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  # compute t tests
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  # sort by p-value
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  # multiple testing correction
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)

## RANDOM FOREST
##################

# store predictors and response separately
train.predictors <- biomarker_train %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

train.response <- biomarker_train %>% pull(group) %>% factor()

# fit RF
train.rf_out <- randomForest(x = train.predictors, 
                       y = train.response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)


panels <- function(n){
  ttest_proteins <- train.ttests_out |> slice_min(p.adj, n=n) |> pull(protein)
  rf_proteins <- train.rf_out$importance |> as_tibble() |>
  mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) |> slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = n) |> pull(protein)
  
  fuzzy <- union(ttest_proteins, rf_proteins)
  hard <- intersect(ttest_proteins, rf_proteins)
  list(hard = hard, fuzzy = fuzzy)
}

evaluate <- function(panel){
  
  fit <- glm(class ~., data = biomarker_train |> mutate(class = (group == "ASD")) |> select(class, all_of(panel)), family = 'binomial')
  
  class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)
  
  biomarker_test |> 
    add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') |>
    mutate(estimate = factor(pred > 0.5, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
           class = (group == "ASD"),
           truth = factor(class, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) |>
    class_metrics(estimate = estimate, truth = truth, pred, event_level = 'second')
}


results <- map(c(5,10, 15, 20, 25, 30), function(n){
  # get the panel of n proteins 
  p <- panels(n)
  
  # iterate through the panels by type
  map(names(p), function(type){
    metrics <- evaluate(p[[type]])
    # if empty then return NULL
    if (is.null(metrics)) return (NULL)
    
    # How many proteins captured by fuzzy or hard intersect
    length <- length(p[[type]])
    
    # Add descriptive columns to differentiate metrics
    metrics |>
      mutate(type = type, n = n, length = length)
  }) |> list_rbind() 
}) |> list_rbind() # combine each list by rows into one data frame

results 

original_metrics
```
